blind.B1: Yes. Treadmill training is the exercise factor (S2.3.p1). RNA-seq is on female mice only, gastrocnemius, n=7 per group: Active (treadmill 6 wk) and Activity Reduction (treadmill 4 wk then 2 wk inactive) carry the exercise factor; Inactive is the sedentary control (S3.7.p1, FIG3 legend, 21 samples = packet A).
blind.B2: Active vs Inactive (71 DEGs), Activity Reduction vs Inactive (40), Activity Reduction vs Active (124); 7 mice per group (FIG3 legend, S3.7.p1). Packet A grp: ACT 7, AR 7, SED 7.
blind.B3: No repeated measures: mice were randomized to three independent groups (S2.3.p1), one muscle sample per mouse, one tissue only. The 'suffix of title' key in packet A is just the replicate number within each group (title 'replicate k'), not an animal ID; the description field M304-M325 is unique per sample. The expression check is not_supported (difference 0.12, status not_supported), consistent with no pairing.
blind.B4: The paper does not say whether comparisons were fitted jointly or pairwise (S2.11.p1 only says DESeq2). Its linked analysis code (DA.p1 GitHub, per the case record) fits each pair separately; I cannot verify that from the paper text.
blind.B5: S2.11.p1: 'Transcripts were considered differentially expressed when FDR<0.05 and the fold change was >0.25 in either direction.' FIG3 legend: 'q < 0.05 and expression change was greater than or equal to 20% in either direction'. Counts S3.7.p1: 71 (Active vs Inactive), 40 (AR vs Inactive), 124 (AR vs Active); 7 transcripts unique to AR.

checks.evidence: Run decision matches B1: treadmill arm present (S2.3.p1), in-vivo, DA.p1 names GSE281849, 21 samples = FIG3 legend n.

grp recoded from characteristics_ch1.2.treatment: Inactive 6 weeks=SED 7, Treadmill trained 6 weeks=ACT 7, trained 4 wk + inactive 2 wk=AR 7; titles and descriptions in packet B agree with the recode; no exclusions; each control is the paper's control for that contrast (SED for ACT and AR, ACT for AR vs ACT).

Contrasts ACT vs SED, AR vs SED, AR vs ACT with the first-named as treatment and the second as control, as in FIG3a-c. The mechanical possible_reversed_contrast flags are false positives: SED is the inactive control and ACT is the active arm, which is the intended reference in AR vs ACT. Named genes (Igfbp5 down in ACT and AR vs SED; Ostn, Ak4, Zfhx4 down and Smyd2, En1 up in AR) go the paper's way (HANDBACK).

No repeated animals (B3). The pairing_key_candidate flag is the within-group replicate number; same-key residual correlation 0.103 vs -0.019, status not_supported. No blocking factor needed; design ~grp is full rank, residual df 18.

Paper text is silent (B4); the run uses pairwise 14-sample fits (as in the authors' code, per the case record) as primary and reports the joint 3-group model as sensitivity (61/15/115). Both fits are reported. Note: joint AR vs SED tests only 1990 genes (15 DEGs), far fewer than the other tables; worth a glance at independent filtering but it does not affect the primary result.

One sex (female), one tissue, one genotype; GEO records no batch or lane; the paper's food-intake week used paired cages but that is not aliased with group in the sequenced data as far as the record shows. The only complete confounding listed is the treatment label with grp itself.

GSE281849_Gastroc_RawCounts.csv.gz is all integers, 0 to 4.68e6, featureCounts per GEO data_processing; NormalizedCounts file rejected; pydeseq2 Wald for raw counts; frac p>0.9 about 0.12 so the p-value histogram is not piled up.

Applied rule padj<0.05 and |log2FC|>0.25 transcribes S2.11.p1 (reading '>0.25' as log2). The FIG3 legend (>=20%, log2 0.263) and the authors' code (>=0.27, padj<=0.05) are recorded as an audit rule and a paper_data_discrepancy. The paper's numbers fit the audit rule better (71/41/126 vs 71/40/124 against 76/45/134). That is the open policy question, recorded rather than ignored. Minor: whether the text's '>0.25' is log2 or linear fold change is not stated in the paper.

Each 'ours vs paper' pair compares the same contrast (ACT vs SED to FIG3a 71, AR vs SED to FIG3b 40, AR vs ACT to FIG3c 124). HANDBACK says counts match almost exactly under the authors' code threshold (71/41/126 vs 71/40/124) and lists the 76/45/134 paper-rule counts next to them; this does not overclaim. It notes GSEA uses Hallmark rather than GO BP, so pathway results are not comparable.
No stop or refusal in this case; all three contrasts and the sensitivity fit completed.

human_items: Open policy: report the paper-stated rule (padj<0.05, |log2FC|>0.25: 76/45/134) or the authors' code rule (padj<=0.05, |log2FC|>=0.27: 71/41/126) as headline; the run reports both, with the paper rule applied.
Optional: joint model AR vs SED has only 1990 tested genes, check whether this is independent filtering or an outlier artefact (sensitivity only).
summary: 分析结果与论文一致：三个独立随机分组（每组7只雌鼠），无重复测量，配对键候选只是组内重复编号，不需要分块。对比方向正确（ACT vs SED、AR vs SED、AR vs ACT），原始计数矩阵配DESeq2，成对拟合为主、联合模型为敏感性分析。阈值按论文方法部分转录，并把作者代码的0.27规则作为审计规则记录，两者的差异属于待决策的开放问题，不是错误；机械标记 possible_reversed_contrast 为误报。总体通过。
